chunks: And whatever in this book is narrated from Khalid ibn Ma' ibn Ma'ad Al-Qalansi, I have transmitted it from my father - may Allah be pleased with him - from Abdullah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from al-Nadr ibn Shu'ayb, from Khalid ibn Ma'ad Al-Qalansi.

key_terms.النُّضْرِ بْنِ شُعَيْبٍ: Al-Nadr ibn Shu'ayb, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.الْحَمِيرِيُّ: Al-Himyari, a nisba indicating lineage or origin
key_terms.خَالِدِ بْنِ مَاعِدٍ الْقَلَنْسِيِّ: Khalid ibn Ma'ad Al-Qalansi, a prominent narrator
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him, a phrase of respect for the father

ai.seo_question: How is the chain of narration for Khalid ibn Ma'ad Al-Qalansi verified in this text?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq clarifies the specific isnad for narrations of Khalid ibn Ma'ad Al-Qalansi, distinguishing them from other chains to ensure precise attribution within his magnum opus, *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*. This meticulous verification reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *tawthiq* (authentication) and the reliability of individual narrators in preserving the Imams' teachings. By explicitly linking the transmission to his father and the chain of trusted scholars, al-Saduq reinforces the textual integrity of the legal rulings derived from these reports.
